label: Diminutives & Augmentatives
description: A 20-question check on the diminutives lessons.

questions.prompt: The diminutive «домик» (little house) is formed from which base word?
questions.explain: The suffix -ик turns «дом» 'house' into «домик» 'little house'.

questions.prompt: What base word does «чашечка» (little cup) come from?
questions.explain: The suffix -ечка shrinks «чашка» 'cup' into «чашечка» 'little cup'.

questions.prompt: The affectionate «сынок» is formed from which word?
questions.explain: The suffix -ок turns «сын» 'son' into «сынок», a warm, tender form of address.

questions.prompt: Which suffix is AUGMENTATIVE, signalling large or coarse size?
questions.explain: The suffix -ище is augmentative: «домище» means a 'huge house', not a small one.

questions.prompt: In «На холме стоит огромный домище», what does the suffix -ище add to «дом»?
questions.explain: The augmentative -ище turns «дом» into «домище» 'huge house', stressing great size.

questions.prompt: The folksy «бабушка» (grandmother) is built from which base?
questions.explain: The folksy suffix -ушка turns «баба» into «бабушка», a warm everyday kin term.

questions.prompt: What base word does the augmentative «ручища» (huge hand) come from?
questions.explain: The augmentative -ища makes «рука» 'hand, arm' into «ручища» 'huge hand'.

questions.prompt: The diminutive «садик» (little garden) is formed from which word?
questions.explain: The suffix -ик makes «сад» 'garden' into «садик» 'little garden'.

questions.prompt: In «Иди ко мне, моя лапонька», what does «лапонька» express?
questions.explain: The suffix -онька turns «лапа» 'paw' into «лапонька» 'darling', a purely affectionate name with no literal meaning.

questions.prompt: What base word does «звёздочка» (little star) come from?
questions.explain: The suffix -очка makes «звезда» 'star' into «звёздочка» 'little star'.

questions.prompt: The augmentative «голосище» is formed from which word?
questions.explain: The augmentative -ище turns «голос» 'voice' into «голосище» 'mighty voice', stressing power and volume.

questions.prompt: Which suffix carries a folksy, fairy-tale or folk-song flavour?
questions.explain: The suffix -ушка/-юшка is folksy: «избушка», «головушка», «соловушка» all have a rustic, lyrical feel.

questions.prompt: The diminutive «диванчик» (little sofa) is formed from which base?
questions.explain: The suffix -чик shrinks «диван» 'sofa' into «диванчик» 'little sofa' with a cosy nuance.

questions.prompt: In «Спи спокойно, моя доченька», what does «доченька» mainly add to «дочь»?
questions.explain: The suffix -енька turns «дочь» 'daughter' into «доченька» 'dear daughter', adding deep affection rather than size.

questions.prompt: The folksy «избушка» (little hut) comes from which word?
questions.explain: The suffix -ушка turns «изба» 'peasant hut' into «избушка», a small, folksy, fairy-tale dwelling.

questions.prompt: What base word does the diminutive «голосок» (little voice) come from?
questions.explain: The suffix -ок shrinks «голос» 'voice' into «голосок», suggesting a thin, small, gentle sound.

questions.prompt: Which suffix would you use to make «кот» 'cat' sound LARGE and rough («котище»)?
questions.explain: The augmentative -ище makes «кот» into «котище» 'huge cat', adding largeness with a rough, comic edge.

questions.prompt: The diminutive «пирожок» (little pie) is formed from which base word?
questions.explain: The suffix -ок makes «пирог» 'pie' into «пирожок», naming a small hand pie with homely warmth.

questions.prompt: In «Болит моя бедная головушка», the suffix -ушка on «голова» gives the word what colouring?
questions.explain: The suffix -ушка makes «голова» into «головушка», a folksy, lyrical, pitying form common in folk songs.

questions.prompt: In the contrast «Не домик, а целый домище!», how do the two suffixes differ?
questions.explain: The diminutive «домик» means a 'little house', while the augmentative «домище» means a 'huge house' — the suffixes reverse the size nuance.
